newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF sets launch of new Ffr, BOBL contracts.
newsitem.headline: MATIF sets launch of new Ffr, BOBL contracts.

text.p: French futures and options exchange Matif SA said on Friday a new French franc five-year bond future would start trading on September 5.
It also in a statement it was launching a five-year mark bond future (BOBL), as well as an option on the contract, and both would start trading on May 16.
Matif SA, the holding company for the MATIF exchange, said the five-year French bond future would have a maturity of four to 5.5 years and a coupon of 4.50 percent.
The exchange said both OATs and BTANs with a residual maturity of between four and 5.5 years and an outstanding of more than 30 billion francs would be eligible for delivery.
It said an option on the five-year future would be launched when the future had reached a level of liquidity judged satisfactory.
MATIF said the BOBL future would have an underlying maturity of 3.5 to five years and a coupon of six percent.
It said German government debt and Treuhandanstalt bonds denominated in marks with a residual maturity of 3.5 to five years and an outstanding of four billion marks would be eligible for delivery.
MATIF said the BOBL futures contract was not intended to rival the BOBL future currently traded on the German DTB exchange in Frankfurt.
It said it was designed to enable investors to cover options positions immediately and to benefit from reduced margin deposits based on their combined positions in the option and the future.
As is the case with current MATIF interest-rate contracts, the BOBL contracts will be traded on Globex after the close of pit-trading.
